keyFindings.description: A kept edit's press-time block ids are dropped from storage on the first reload, so a second reload brings back 422 KEY_REUSED. `keep` recomputes the ids with carriedIds(request), which reads edit.blocks. `restoredEdit` sets blocks: undefined and holds the ids only in its save closure. Writes.#update re-keeps the detail through kind.keep on every update, including #resume (write-store.ts:717, 733, 982-983). So the restored write is saved back as {id} alone. A Retry after a second reload, or a Retry that a reload interrupts, goes under the same key (SendInterruptedError → retriesUnderItsKey) with {body} only, and the server answers 422 KEY_REUSED. Both thermonuclear agents reproduced this with scratch probes. The new test reloads only once. The `followed ?? carried` fallback at :258 shows the same split: sendAttempt passes carriedIds(sent), which is always undefined for a restored edit. Fix: keep the ids as data that both keep and sendAttempt read, for example a `carried` field on SentRequest.edit worked out once at the press, which keep writes and restore reads back. Add a two-reload (or reload-interrupts-Retry) test.
